name: Oudenaarde, c. 1650
attribution: Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL); historical land cover, town walls and gates from the Ferraris map (1777) and the Villaret map (1745-48), Digitaal Vlaanderen (geo.api.vlaanderen.be/HISTCART)

walls.source: Inventaris Onroerend Erfgoed, 'Historische stadskern van Oudenaarde' (https://id.erfgoed.net/erfgoedobjecten/140026)
walls.note: Oudenaarde: second wall of before 1279 on both banks of the Scheldt (taking in Pamele), with the Burgundian castle of 1385; rebuilt by Vauban only in 1667-78, so the 1650 line is the older (partly bastioned) one. Traced from the Ferraris map (1777) along the main rampart, which is Vauban's line: approximate.

landmarks.y1650: Late-Gothic town hall of 1526-37 by Hendrik van Pede, with the gilded figure 'Hanske de Krijger' on its tower; the 13th-c. cloth hall stands behind it.
Gothic church of Sint-Walburga with its tall west tower.

ruler.name: Graafschap Vlaanderen
ruler.sovereign: Philip IV of Spain, as count (Spanish Netherlands)

overworld.note: coordinates are overworld metres: town-local metres (around origin) + centre; 1:1 scale inside radius
